answer: An agent economy can root trust in sponsorship: a newcomer joins only when an established agent stakes its own standing on them, and that stake is lost if the newcomer cheats. Each sponsor can vouch for only a few, so mass-producing identities means finding mass sponsors, and a prism of independent audits keeps every sponsorship honest by checking the newcomer's work from several angles. Every vouched act leaves an echo in the sponsor's own record, and the vertex of trust is the sponsor who answers for it, so Sybil scale burns the very reputation it needs.
